title: More Than Expected
body:
I wanted something thin, fast, a convertible, with backlit keys, and a touch screen. Honestly, I got more than what I expected. I wasn't expecting a Pen, but one was included in the box. 

The price was just right because of the promotion, and I saved a significant amount.

The 2-in-1  is portable, fast, and beautiful. Don't get me started on the screen and color depth with the 3k OLED.

I love it, love it, love it...

title: No more bulky bags and cords!
body: I love my new omnibook! It is compact, thin, light, and the battery lasts all day - i dont wven pack ny charger going to uni, and I am on it all day! The screen is quite good for short notes with the pen (sold separately), so its thr perfect study companion. I also love that it boots up so quickly, i can be confident to just shut it down and it springs to action the next day. The only annoying thing ill say is the facial recognition is quite buggy and i have to keep resetting it. Even when i use my code instead it tells me to reset my facial recognition each time i open it up, which gets annoying.

title: Unsure about it, for now
body: I owned 2x HP Spectres before purchasing the HP OmniBook X Flip. Both lasted for years, until the SSD in my latest model died on me, forcing me to buy a new laptop. Up until that point I loved HP and had no issues at all. As soon as I setup my HP OmniBook X Flip I started to encounter problems such as the screen not waking up from sleep mode and the Bluetooth not working properly with my wireless earphones. I spent hours working with the HP Support team, that has been amazing, and fixed the issues, but part of me thinks I might have bought a lemon. Fingers crossed these will be the only issues I will ever have with this new laptop.
